proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
W=\operatorname{PP}_{\mathcal S,L}(Y_0)
=\{X_{-\gamma}\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z,
\qquad w_x=(x,z),\quad x\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The disjoint union follows from \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\) and the definition of \(Z\).  By \(\text{ass:strict-observed-positivity}\), every cell of \(p\) on \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\) has positive mass.  Each assignment \(W=w_x\) has at least one full-window extension, and its probability is the sum of the positive probabilities of all such extensions.  Therefore
\[
p(W=w_x)>0,\qquad x\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus every observational conditional expectation below is well defined; equation (2) is the division condition used in conditioning.

We first compare the directed part of a refinement with the supergraph.  If \((u,s)\to(v,t)\in E_G^{\to}\), then \(u\to v\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\) by \(\text{ass:exact-summary-projection}\), and \(1\le t-s\le L\) by \(\text{ass:positive-bounded-directed-lags}\).  Hence the definition of \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) gives
\[
E_G^{\to}\subseteq E_D
\quad\text{and consequently}\quad
\operatorname{An}_G(A)\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(A)
\quad(A\subseteq\mathcal W_H).
\tag{3}
\]
Every directed edge in \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) strictly increases its time coordinate, so this directed graph is acyclic.  The same positive-lag property makes \(Y_0\) terminal in the observed window: an edge \(Y_0\to(C,t)\) would require \(t\ge1\), whereas \(t\in\mathbb T_H\) implies \(t\le0\).  In particular,
\[
Y_0\notin\operatorname{An}_G(W).
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed, membership in the reflexive ancestral closure would give a directed path from \(Y_0\) to a vertex of \(W\), while \(W\) consists of vertices at strictly negative times.

If \((B,s)\in\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)\), then \((B,s)\to(Y,0)\in E_G^{\to}\).  The two structural assumptions just used give \(B\to Y\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\) and \(1\le -s\le L\).  By the definition of the positive-lag possible-parent set,
\[
\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)\subseteq W.
\tag{5}
\]

We next isolate the exogenous blocks.  For \(v\in\mathcal W_H\), let
\[
\mathcal I_G(v)=\bigl\{\{v\}\bigr\}\cup
\bigl\{a\in E_G^{\leftrightarrow}:v\in a\bigr\},
\qquad
\mathcal E_G(A)=\bigcup_{v\in\operatorname{An}_G(A)}\mathcal I_G(v).
\tag{6}
\]
Because \(G\) is a finite ADMG, its directed part has a topological ordering.  Induction in that ordering using \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\) shows that \(V_A\) is a deterministic function of \((U_a:a\in\mathcal E_G(A))\): at a vertex \(v\), the recursion introduces only factors indexed by \(\mathcal I_G(v)\), and the induction hypotheses for its directed parents introduce factors incident to directed ancestors of \(v\).  Apply this fact with \(A=W\).

We claim
\[
\mathcal I_G(Y_0)\cap\mathcal E_G(W)=\varnothing.
\tag{7}
\]
For the private index \(\{Y_0\}\), membership in \(\mathcal E_G(W)\) would force \(Y_0\in\operatorname{An}_G(W)\), contrary to (4).  Now let a pairwise index \(a=\{Y_0,b\}\in E_G^{\leftrightarrow}\) belong to \(\mathcal E_G(W)\).  By (6), at least one endpoint of \(a\) belongs to \(\operatorname{An}_G(W)\).  Equation (4) excludes \(Y_0\), hence \(b\in\operatorname{An}_G(W)\).  By (3), \(b\in\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W)\).  Moreover, the refinement definition gives \(E_G^{\leftrightarrow}\subseteq\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\), so \(\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\).  This contradicts condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\), proving (7).  Notice that this is the exact latent-block check: an edge latent incident to \(Y_0\) can enter the graphical recursive determination of \(W\) only through its other endpoint, and that endpoint must be a directed ancestor of \(W\).

Let \(U_Y=(U_a:a\in\mathcal I_G(Y_0))\) and \(U_W=(U_a:a\in\mathcal E_G(W))\).  The index sets are disjoint by (7).  The entire finite latent family is mutually independent by \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\); factorization of its joint mass function therefore gives \(U_Y\perp U_W\).  Since \(V_W\) is a deterministic function of \(U_W\),
\[
U_Y\perp V_W.
\tag{8}
\]
This step allows several independent edge latents to overlap at an observed vertex; it uses independence of distinct latent factors, not disjointness of their observed children.

By \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\) and (5), the terminal structural equation is
\[
Y_0=f_{Y_0}\!\left(V_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},U_Y\right),
\qquad \operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)\subseteq W.
\tag{9}
\]
For \(x\in\{0,1\}\), equations (2), (8), and (9), together with \(\text{ass:observed-law-compatibility}\), imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_p[Y_0\mid W=w_x]
&=\sum_u f_{Y_0}\!\left((w_x)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},u\right)
  \Pr_{\mathcal M}(U_Y=u\mid W=w_x)\\
&=\sum_u f_{Y_0}\!\left((w_x)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},u\right)
  \Pr_{\mathcal M}(U_Y=u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Under \(\operatorname{do}(W=w_x)\), all actual parents in (5) are fixed at their entries in \(w_x\), while the intervention leaves the exogenous law unchanged.  Truncating the structural recursion at the intervened coordinates and using (9) therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal M}[Y_0\mid\operatorname{do}(W=w_x)]
=\sum_u f_{Y_0}\!\left((w_x)_{\operatorname{pa}_G(Y_0)},u\right)
  \Pr_{\mathcal M}(U_Y=u).
\tag{11}
\]
Comparison of (10) and (11), followed by (1), proves the two conditional-mean equalities in the statement.  Subtracting the case \(x=0\) from the case \(x=1\), and using \(\text{def:micro-cde}\) and the definition of \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\), proves \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\).

Finally, condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is load-bearing for this argument and cannot simply be omitted.  Take \(H=L=\gamma=1\), directed edge \(X_{-1}\to Y_0\), and bidirected edge \(X_{-1}\leftrightarrow Y_0\).  Then \(W=\{X_{-1}\}\), and the other endpoint \(X_{-1}\) belongs to the reflexive closure \(\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W)\), so \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) fails.  Let the shared edge latent \(U\) be fair, let independent private noises satisfy \(E_X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e)\) and \(E_Y\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\delta)\), where \(e,\delta\in(0,1/2)\), and set
\[
X_{-1}=U\mathbin\oplus E_X,
\qquad
Y_0=(X_{-1}\mathbin\lor U)\mathbin\oplus E_Y.
\tag{12}
\]
Give every remaining window vertex an independent private Bernoulli noise with parameter in \((0,1)\).  For each observed cell, choosing a value of \(U\) and then the uniquely required private-noise values gives a latent configuration of positive mass, so the induced observed law is strictly positive.  Directly,
\[
\begin{aligned}
q(\mathcal M)
&=(1-\delta)-\frac12=\frac{1-2\delta}{2},\\
\mathbb E[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=1]-\mathbb E[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=0]
&=(1-\delta)-\bigl(\delta+(1-2\delta)e\bigr)
=(1-2\delta)(1-e).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The two quantities differ because \(e\ne1/2\).  This exact two-node calculation verifies failure when an incident edge latent can enter the controlled parent itself.

By \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\),
\[
W=\{X_{-\gamma}\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z.
\tag{14}
\]
Strict observed positivity implies \(p(W=(x,z))>0\) for both \(x\in\{0,1\}\), by the summation-over-full-cells argument in equations (1)--(2) of \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\).  Hence \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\) is well defined.

Fix an arbitrary \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is independent of the chosen refinement and is exactly the premise of \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\).  Fiber membership supplies that lemma's structural, factorization, graph-compatibility, and observed-law hypotheses.  The lemma therefore gives
\[
q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{15}
\]
Because the fiber member was arbitrary, \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) gives
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\subseteq\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{16}
\]
The assumed nonemptiness of \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\) supplies at least one pair \((G,\mathcal M)\) in the fiber.  Equation (15) for that pair proves the reverse inclusion in (16), and hence
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{17}
\]
The infimum and supremum of the nonempty singleton in (17) both equal its unique element.  The endpoint definitions in \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) thus yield
\[
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{18}
\]

We now compare the new micro condition with the former label-level condition.  Suppose the former condition holds, and assume for contradiction that some \(b=(B,s)\) satisfies
\[
\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S),
\qquad
b\in\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W).
\tag{19}
\]
The first relation in (19) implies \(Y\leftrightarrow B\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow}\).  The second gives a directed path in \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) from \(b\) to some \(w=(C,-\ell)\in W\), with a length-zero path permitted.  Projection of a positive-length path gives a directed summary walk from \(B\) to \(C\); for a length-zero path, \(B=C\).  Since \(w\in W\), the definition of \(W\) gives \(C\to Y\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\).  Concatenation, followed by deletion of repetitions if necessary, makes \(B\) a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).  This contradicts the former condition.  Thus the former label-level condition implies \(\mathrm{(MC)}\).

The implication is strict.  Set \(H=L=\gamma=1\), take three distinct labels \(B,X,Y\), and let the summary graph have exactly the directed edges
\[
B\to X,\qquad X\to Y,
\tag{19a}
\]
and the bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\).  The bounded-window supergraph then has exactly
\[
B_{-1}\to X_0,
\qquad
X_{-1}\to Y_0.
\tag{20}
\]
Consequently \(W=\{X_{-1}\}\) and
\[
\operatorname{An}_{D_{1,1}(\mathcal S)}(W)=\{X_{-1}\}.
\tag{21}
\]
The admissible endpoints paired with \(Y_0\) are \(B_{-1}\) and \(B_0\), neither of which belongs to (21); hence \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) holds.  On the other hand, \(B\to X\to Y\), so the summary bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) violates the former label-level exclusion.

It remains to verify that this graphical gain is not vacuous.  Let \(G^{\dagger}\) contain the two directed edges in (20) and the single bidirected edge \(Y_0\leftrightarrow B_{-1}\).  This graph has the required positive lag, its bidirected edge belongs to \(\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\), and its exact summary projection is \(\mathcal S\).  Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r)\) be the edge latent, and let the six private noises \(E_{B,-1},E_{B,0},E_{X,-1},E_{X,0},E_{Y,-1},E_{Y,0}\) be mutually independent of \(U\), each with both states of positive probability.  Define
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
B_{-1}=U\mathbin\oplus E_{B,-1},
&B_0=E_{B,0},
&X_{-1}=E_{X,-1},\\
X_0=B_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{X,0},
&Y_{-1}=E_{Y,-1},
&Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin\oplus U\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}.
\end{array}
\tag{22}
\]
These equations satisfy \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\), and their private and pairwise exogenous variables satisfy \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\).  For any prescribed observed six-bit cell, fix \(U=0\) and solve (22) successively for the six private noises.  The resulting latent configuration has positive probability, so the induced law \(p^{\dagger}\) is strictly positive.  Thus \((G^{\dagger},\mathcal M^{\dagger})\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,1,1,p^{\dagger})\), proving nonemptiness.

For a quantitative check, take \(r=1/4\) and \(\Pr(E_{Y,0}=1)=1/4\).  Then
\[
\eta:=\Pr(U\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}=1)
=r+\frac14-2r\frac14=\frac38.
\tag{23}
\]
Since \(X_{-1}=E_{X,-1}\) is independent of \((U,E_{Y,0})\), both the interventional and observational conditional contrasts in this model equal
\[
(1-\eta)-\eta=1-2\eta=\frac14.
\tag{24}
\]
Equations (20)--(24) are the requested strict-gain stress test: the summary-level ancestor exclusion fails, the exact bounded-window micro condition holds, the observed law has full support, and adjustment agrees with the nonzero causal contrast.

For completeness, directed cycles through \(Y\) are genuinely admitted.  With \(H=L=\gamma=1\), take the two-label summary with directed edges \(X\to Y\) and \(Y\to X\) and no bidirected edges.  Its refinement has directed edges \(X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(Y_{-1}\to X_0\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is vacuous.  With mutually independent private noises having both states of positive probability, set
\[
X_{-1}=E_{X,-1},\qquad Y_{-1}=E_{Y,-1},\qquad
X_0=Y_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{X,0},\qquad
Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}.
\tag{25}
\]
For any observed four-bit cell, the corresponding private-noise vector is obtained uniquely from (25) and has positive probability.  Thus the fiber contains a strictly positive model although the summary has the directed cycle \(X\to Y\to X\).  Its full-time directed graph is acyclic because every edge advances time.

proposed.name: Bounded positive-lag supergraph and micro ancestral closure
proposed.construction:
Define the bounded positive-lag directed supergraph on the observed window by
\[
D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)=(\mathcal W_H,E_D),
\qquad
(u,s)\to(v,t)\in E_D
\Longleftrightarrow
\bigl(u\to v\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to},\ s,t\in\mathbb T_H,\ 1\le t-s\le L\bigr).
\]
Put
\[
W=\operatorname{PP}_{\mathcal S,L}(Y_0).
\]
For every \(A\subseteq\mathcal W_H\), its reflexive directed ancestral closure in \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) is
\[
\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(A)
=\bigl\{a\in\mathcal W_H:\text{there are }w\in A\text{ and a directed path }a\to\cdots\to w\text{ in }D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\bigr\},
\]
where a path of length zero is allowed, so \(A\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(A)\).

Their causal-order linear program optimizes counterfactual queries over arbitrary masses on complete deterministic response signatures consistent with the supplied order and reconstructs attaining SCMs.
Proposition 3.1 preserves a canonical-domain linear program by pushing an unrestricted simplex mass to equivalence cells and selecting one raw representative per cell for the reverse lift.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite binary process is observed through a bounded window and a lag-abstracted directed and bidirected summary graph. Directed effects occur only at positive lags through \(L\), while bidirected dependence may span any summary-compatible pair of time points in the observed \(H\)-window. The sharp controlled-micro-direct-effect envelope is the attained range of a finite union of raw semi-Markovian response-function polynomial programs, and a total exact certifier returns incompatibility certificates or isolated algebraic endpoints with attaining SCMs. Positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal, so controlling its full possible-parent set identifies the effect by the Ferreira--Assaad adjustment contrast whenever no admissible endpoint paired bidirectedly with \(Y_0\) lies in the reflexive ancestry of that parent set in the bounded positive-lag supergraph. This exact micro condition permits directed summary cycles through \(Y\) and strictly improves the label-level summary-ancestor exclusion, as witnessed by the one-lag summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\). The envelope is strictly narrower on a relative-open temporal-instrument family than a complete temporal-order comparator. Simultaneous multinomial regions support tie-aware inference. Exact analysis of the response-signature quotient supplies a general factor-incidence test and a quotient-size bound, while an explicit edge-latent-chain certificate shows that unrestricted quotient-simplex masses can enlarge the independent-edge-latent image; the endpoint compiler therefore retains the raw product parameterization in general.

project_justification.gap: Existing summary-graph adjustment conditions are formulated at label level for models that may contain contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws. They do not isolate which time-stamped endpoint of a latent incident to terminal \(Y_0\) can actually enter the recursive determination of the controlled possible-parent vector in a bounded positive-lag window. Existing automated bounds take one fixed graph, and unrestricted response-signature quotient simplexes need not preserve nonlinear independent-edge-latent product images.
project_justification.niche: The positive-directed-lag bound makes the full-time refinement set finite and makes the end-of-window outcome terminal, while summary-compatible bidirected lags remain unrestricted inside the observed window. The bounded positive-lag supergraph gives an exact finite-window ancestry test for overlap between the terminal outcome latent block and the controlled possible-parent recursion. Binary canonical response functions turn each fixed-refinement image into a compact semialgebraic set, and the complete temporal-order common-latent model supplies a coherent graph-free outer comparator.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp raw compiler and a total exact certifier; proves adjustment and envelope collapse under the exact bounded-window micro-ancestry condition; and exhibits the strict-gain one-lag summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), which the former label-level condition rejects even though its only \(B\to X\) placement cannot affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\). It also permits directed summary cycles through the outcome label and embeds every refinement into the complete order-only comparator. Explicit rational primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior ledger certify relative-open strict tightening. One multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts. For response-signature compression, the project proves exact factorized push-forward fidelity, gives a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic factor-incidence test and a quotient-size bound, and exhibits an exact separating certificate showing why unrestricted quotient-simplex masses cannot replace the raw product parameterization in general.

prose_updates.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem 9) provide the summary-graph controlled-micro-direct-effect setup and adjustment expression. In the present finite-window binary semi-Markovian class with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents, strict positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal. The relevant exclusion can therefore be stated at the finer time-stamped level: no admissible endpoint paired bidirectedly with \(Y_0\) may lie in the reflexive ancestry of the controlled possible-parent set in the bounded positive-lag supergraph. This condition removes both the singleton strongly connected component requirement and the conservative exclusion of every summary bidirected edge to a summary ancestor. The gain is strict: with \(H=L=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), the sole \(B_{-1}\to X_0\) placement is too late to affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\), so adjustment holds although \(B\) is a summary ancestor of \(Y\). This is an extension within the present model class, not a claim that the present scope contains Ferreira--Assaad's: they permit contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, whereas this paper excludes instantaneous directed effects and imposes independent pairwise-edge-latent factorization. Duarte et al. prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper studies finite-window binary SCMs with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents. It excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\), but places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags inside the observed \(H\)-window; Ferreira--Assaad allow contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, so the positive-lag adjustment theorem is an extension only within the present distinct scope. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected. No stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the raw response-weight dimension and is a certificate engine, not a polynomial-time method. Empty fibers receive exact branchwise infeasibility certificates; nonempty fibers receive attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. Every graph refinement embeds in the complete temporal-order common-latent comparator, but unrestricted comparator masses are not asserted to respect missing bidirected edges. Strict tightening is relative to positive laws with a nonempty summary-graph fiber. The quotient question is resolved rather than left open: factorized push-forward is exact, a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic test characterizes when the unrestricted quotient simplex is also exact, a finite quotient-size bound is proved, and the edge-latent-chain witness shows that unrestricted quotienting fails in general. Accordingly the main compiler remains unquotiented unless the exact test certifies a particular graph. When the refinement class is a singleton the construction reduces to a fixed-graph response program. More generally, positive-lag terminality collapses the envelope to the adjustment contrast whenever no admissible bidirected endpoint paired with \(Y_0\) belongs to the reflexive bounded-window ancestry of the controlled possible-parent set; this exact micro condition permits summary cycles through \(Y\) and may hold even when \(Y\) is bidirected with a summary ancestor.
